newsitem.title: UK: Newman Tonks seen costing FKI 200 mln stg.
newsitem.headline: Newman Tonks seen costing FKI 200 mln stg.

text.p: Acquisitive British engineering group FKI Plc would probably have to pay in excess of 200 million pounds ($331 million) if it goes ahead and snaps up building supplier Newman Tonks Group Plc, analysts said on Monday.

"I don't think people should be looking at much more than 130 pence a share. There is around 40 million pounds of debt associated with it, which would mean paying just over 200 million," said Paul Compton at investment bank Merrill Lynch.
Newman Tonks shares shot ahead today after it revealed it might receive a bid offer from FKI.
By 1111 GMT, shares in the company had risen 26-1/2p to stand at 129p, well above its year low of 98p.
"It looks like people think it is a done deal given the share price reaction," said analyst Compton.

The attraction of Newman for the diversified engineering group is the potential the acquisition would give it to expand its already profitable hardware operations to Europe from the United States, sector analysts said.
"It would be regarded as a geographically complementary fit for the extension of their hardware operations," said Andy Chambers, an analyst at Societe Generale Strauss Turnbull.
Analysts said FKI would be buying around 300 million of sales for around 200 million. Around one third of FKI's profits are currently derived from its hardware operations.
"Whether or not there are any real benefits to be derived from being international in the business is hard to say," said Compton at Merrill Lynch.

FKI said in November that it would continue to focus on new acquisitions despite its recent buying spree which has seen it pay out some 235 million pounds since August for Italian firm Marelli Motori and the Hawker Siddeley Electric power group.

"It is a bit like waiting for a bus, FKI were waiting for a good deal for about two years then all of a sudden three of them have come along at once, they have jumped on two and might now get on Newman," said Compton at Merrill Lynch.
Analysts expect that the purchase price for Newman would probably be satisfied with a paper and cash deal given FKI's 60 percent plus gearing ratio.

However, they noted that interest cover, a measure of the company's ability to pay interest on borrowings using profits for the year, is comfortable at around nine times for next year. ($1=.6043 Pound)
